title: RuleEvalResult
description: Output of `rule eval` — the runtime verdict for ONE rule against a document INSTANCE, either a stored `<rulePathInModel>` or a non-stored `--condition`/`--field` candidate. Both forms return this identical shape. FOUR verdicts, and `fired:false` is three of them: `fired` (a violation), `passed` (evaluated, condition false), `suppressed` (never evaluated — a referenced field is formally invalid, so reporting a pass would mislead), `unsupported` (a construct the engine does not model, e.g. a CustomCondition with no registered impl). A `fired` verdict additionally publishes the firing MESSAGE's own channels — `code`, `field`, `severity`, `type`, `message`, `referenced`, and (for an omission) `fillToFix` — the same keys and the same meanings as one `model eval` `messages[]` entry, so one message parser reads both. It reports the FIRST firing only: a rule that violates several rows of its iteration scope yields one message here, where `model eval` yields one per row. The INPUT --instance shape is NOT restated here — it is `document-instance.schema.json`, served as the `docInput` half of `dmtool schema rule eval`.

rule.description: the evaluated rule's full slash-path; a candidate reports the in-memory name it was given (`<group>/EvalRuleCandidate`), which is never written to the model

fired.description: whether the rule fired (true iff `verdict` is `fired`). Kept beside `verdict` because it is the one-bit question most callers ask, but it does NOT distinguish the three false cases — read `verdict` for that

verdict.description: fired | passed | suppressed | unsupported (see the description)

code.description: (fired only) the rule's error code — for a candidate, whatever `--code` supplied

field.description: (fired only) the offending field's address, in the message-address form documented under `messages[].field` in `schema model eval`: canonical A12 (no leading slash, `[1]` omitted) when it names one cell, the interpreter house form otherwise. Test the leading slash to tell the two apart

type.description: (fired only) the firing's polarity. A semantic observable, not presentation: for `FieldValuesNotUnique` it is the only thing distinguishing a filtered from an unfiltered firing on identical data — a reached `Having` on the starred operand escalates the firing to OMISSION_ERROR where the unfiltered form reports VALUE_ERROR

message.description: (fired only) the INTERPOLATED end-user text — the authored message with its $Field$/$Field.value$ tokens resolved against this document. A candidate carries no message template, so it renders its in-memory name, which is the `--code` value

referenced.description: (fired only) the fields the rule READ — its operands (A12's referencedFields). Same address contract as `field`, decided per address: a starred operand consumed as a whole column names a set of cells, so it renders as the house form beside an exact `field`

fillToFix.description: (fired with `type: OMISSION_ERROR`) the operand fields that can cause the omission, filled ones included (the kernel's refOmissionErrorResponsible); an operand read only by a presence check such as `FieldFilled` is referenced but never listed here. Absent for a value error. Same address contract as `field`

suppressedBy.description: (suppressed only) the referenced fields whose formally-invalid values kept the rule from being evaluated

field.description: the offending cell, as a canonical A12 instance pointer (no leading slash, `[1]` omitted). Every level is resolved by construction here, so unlike a message address this one is always canonical

formalErrorCode.description: the kernel formal-check code that made the value invalid, e.g. datumFormatFalsch

unsupported.description: (unsupported only) what the engine could not evaluate — reported rather than passed off as a clean `passed` (G29). `--strict-custom` turns this into a refusal (exit 2)

name.description: what could not be evaluated — read it according to `subject`, since the two kinds are different addresses

subject.description: element = a model path (a rule/computation/field declaration, no repetition); cell = a canonical A12 instance pointer to a document cell
